question: Which of the following Gods acquires a new epithet ‘Lord of the Plough’ in the later Vedic period?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indra:-**

 
 
• **The god Indra acquires the epithet "Lord of the Plough" in the later Vedic period. **
 
• This epithet reflects the increasing importance of agriculture in Vedic society during this time.
 
• Indra was already associated with rain and fertility, so it was natural for him to also become associated with the tools of agriculture.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Varuna:-**

 
 
• **It is the god of the sky, waters, and the cosmic order. He is the upholder of morality and justice. **
 
• He is often depicted as a man with four arms, riding a white elephant.
 
 
 
• **Brahma:-**
 
 
• **It is the god of creation. He is the one who brought the universe into existence. **
 
• He is often depicted as a four-faced man with a white beard.
 
 
 
• **Vishnu:-**
 
 
• **It is the god of preservation. He is the one who maintains the balance of the universe. **
 
• He is often depicted as a man with four arms, holding a conch shell, a chakra, a mace, and a lotus flower.
